scope: Theorem 4.7 (Fixed-parameter subcubic perfect-matching search) of the manuscript “Almost-Linear-Time Maximum-Cardinality Matching in General Graphs” (preprints/Almost-Linear-Time-Maximum-Cardinality-Matching-in-Sparse-General-Graphs-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 120 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3cce6ec72ecade69), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 30-31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the integers a ≥ 1000 and fixed reliability parameters 0 ≤ σ ≤ a + 1, the construction defines a uniform randomized algorithm on loopless subcubic graphs with identified edge copies and N ≤ S vertices. Every computation halts 30 with a checked perfect matching, a negative answer, or a suspension. It has no false positive. For each fixed input with a perfect matching, the probability of a negative answer is at most 2−σ S−5 . (4.23) This statement bounds erroneous answers, not suspensions, and holds conditionally for adaptive invocations with fresh randomness and valid prerequisites. For every sufficiently large fixed a and fixed admissible σ, there is no suspension on any path at all sufficiently large S. The total time on every path is then S1+O(1/a)+oa(1) , (4.24) where the exponent coefficients in O(1/a) are absolute. All initialization, physical data movement, arithmetic, random bits, and explicit witness writing are included.
